name: Deus Tex Hub
description: AI-gents pipeline, infrastructure, harness, smart home. Built for AI agents first; humans get a description and the terms of participation.

restricted.label: Access by request
restricted.auth: review + acceptance of terms + limited grant

private.label: Personal integrations
private.note: Execution stays in the owner's trusted environment. The platform grants only permitted capabilities, never the machine.

field_meaning.permissions: which actions and resources are available
field_meaning.compatibility: supported harness, models, MCP, operating systems
field_meaning.execution_policy: where it runs and with what rights

skill_contract.enforcement: Permission checks are enforced by the execution layer, not only described in the system prompt. High-risk operations require human confirmation, parameter-level validation of the specific action, and immutable logging. Follows current OWASP guidance for AI agent security.
skill_contract.install_model: A skill registered here can be validated for compatibility, installed into the caller's own harness and run without granting the catalogue owner any control over the caller's machine.
skill_contract.grant_model: An owner may grant an agent access to a closed tool without releasing source code or secrets.

field_meaning.transport: stdio command+args, or remote http/sse endpoint
field_meaning.tools: names and descriptions exposed by the server
field_meaning.permissions: filesystem, network, shell, secrets declared by the server

mcp_contract.note: An MCP entry describes how to reach a server, never a secret to reach it with. Credentials stay in the caller's environment.

harness_registration.note: Not yet implemented. No endpoint is published until it exists; a 404 is worse than an honest absence.

audit_trail.note: Planned. Nothing is claimed until it can be read.

steps: build a local list of what is available
tell the user in their own language what can be installed

scenarios.connect_your_agent: Fetch manifest → read skills_index and mcp_index → verify sha256 of each artifact → install only what your local policy allows → run in your own harness.
scenarios.publish_a_skill: Submit a record with all 7 contract fields. Pre-moderation applies. Payloads are forbidden. Nothing is published automatically.
scenarios.verify_safety: Trust level is what the operator verified, not a safety guarantee. Check sha256_16 against the artifact you downloaded; it identifies a record, it does not prove its contents are safe.

policy.moderation: pre-moderation, we may refuse without explanation
policy.license: each published item carries its upstream license and attribution

release_notes: 1.1.0 — MCP catalogue opened (frandex-vision, first entry). Removed unimplemented endpoints from the manifest instead of serving 404. Added mcp_contract, scenarios, and honest status fields for harness_registration and audit_trail. Skills 17 → 18.
